subject: BAA eligibility for clinical analytics pipeline — PHI tokenization & retention
messages:
From: Sara Beck <sara@baastream.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inquiry — BAA coverage for clinical pipeline (tokenization + retention)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off a pilot at Baastream to use Redwood for a clinical analytics feature that will surface near-real-time alerts for enrolled clinics. A couple of clarifying questions before we scope a BAA: 

1) Scope: Our ingestion pipeline currently pushes structured EHR extracts and free-text clinician notes to a preprocessing stage. Which parts of Redwood's hosted inference flow would you consider "processing PHI" under a standard BAA? Specifically, does real-time inference (no logs persisted) qualify as handling PHI, and how do ephemeral KV caches factor into that?

2) Tokenization/PII redaction: We currently pseudonymize names and MRNs before sending, but clinician notes still contain free-text PHI (addresses, meds). Can Redwood apply tokenization/PII redaction on the edge prior to entering the model runtime, or would that live on our side?

3) Retention: Our compliance team requires that any request-level data that could be re-identified be retained no longer than 30 days unless a BAA extends that window. What retention guarantees (default) does hosted API provide, and what options exist under Dedicated or Private?

4) Evidence: We will need a short artifact list to start our legal review: SOC 2 scope (is logging excluded), copy of the standard BAA, and a high-level dataflow diagram showing which Redwood services touch request payloads.

Can you point me at a short answers + artifacts pack, and advise if we should be looking at Redwood Dedicated or Private for an initial pilot?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m if easier.

Sara
Director of Product
Baastream

-----
Attachment: baastream-dataflow-20261130.png (image/png) — diagram of our ingestion flow (client -> preprocessing -> Redwood hosted API)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Beck <sara@baastream.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — BAA coverage for clinical pipeline (tokenization + retention)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear questions and the diagram, that helps. Quick summary up front: yes, Redwood can enter a BAA for this workload; the right deployment depends on your risk/controls and the level of evidence you need. Below are short answers and next steps; Dylan and Marcus are looped for technical and contract specifics.

Short answers:
- Scope: Any request payload processed by our inference runtime is considered TA ("processing PHI") under the BAA. Ephemeral KV caches used for active sequences are treated as in-memory only and not persisted to long-term logs by default, but they are still in-scope for the BAA.
- Tokenization/redaction: We offer a lightweight edge filter (policy-based PII scrubbing) as an optional integration for Hosted that runs before the request enters the model path. For high-assurance redaction we recommend combining edge pseudonymization on your side + our scrubber.
- Retention: Hosted default retention (without BAA) is 7 days for temporary request logs and 90 days for aggregated telemetry. Under a BAA we can negotiate a 30-day request retention window or shorter; Dedicated/Private allow you to set retention to meet your regulatory needs (including 0-days for request logs if you choose).
- Evidence: I attached a short BAA summary and a one-page dataflow map. Marcus will follow up with SOC 2 scope and the evidence pack.

Next steps:
1) Marcus: can you confirm SOC 2 scope (are request logs included in our Type II controls?) and attach the evidence pack we give to healthcare pilots.
2) Dylan: quick note on the edge scrubber — what's the recommended config for clinician notes (NLP-based PHI redaction + allowlist for meds)?
3) Sara/Roberto: if we all agree, let's schedule a 30-min call this week to align on minimal pilot scope and retention. I'll bring the draft BAA.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment: redwood-baa-summary.pdf (application/pdf) — one-page summary of BAA coverage and standard exceptions
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sara Beck <sara@baastream.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — BAA coverage for clinical pipeline (tokenization + retention)

Hi all — quick SOC 2 / evidence notes:

- SOC 2: Our Type II report covers the Redwood Console, orchestration/control plane, and the serving runtime availability and change management controls. Request-level application logs are excluded from the standard public SOC 2 bundle by default because many customers require custom retention; however, we provide a tailored SOC 2 addendum and a customer-facing artifact pack for healthcare pilots that includes:
  * SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted)
  * PenTest summary (latest quarter)
  * Dataflow diagram (we can add a customer-specific overlay)
  * Config checklist for Dedicated/Private (retention, KMS integration, audit log retention)

- Evidence delivery: We can upload the artifact pack to the HubSpot company record and share a signed NDA cover if you want the full redacted report.

- Suggested path for Baastream pilot: start on Hosted with the edge-filter and a 30-day retention negotiated in the BAA for request logs. If the clinic customers need stricter controls (0-day logs, dedicated KMS, or on-prem), we can transition to Dedicated in the rollout.

I'll prepare the evidence pack and a redacted SOC 2 summary by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Director, Security and Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sara Beck <sara@baastream.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — BAA coverage for clinical pipeline (tokenization + retention)

Sara, Hannah — quick engineering detail on the edge scrubber and KV cache behavior: 

- Edge scrubber: Our recommended config for free-text clinician notes is a two-stage pipeline: 1) regex/heuristic scrub (MRNs, SSNs, phone numbers, addresses) followed by 2) ML-based NER tuned for PHI to catch names, dates, and rare entities. We expose that as a lightweight sidecar you can run in your preprocessing cluster; if you prefer, we can host it as an optional pre-processing layer for Hosted but that increases the paperwork/attestation.

- KV cache: The inference runtime keeps per-session KV in-memory only for active sequences. By default that data is not written to disk or long-term logs; for additional assurance we offer an in-memory encryption flag and strict TTLs. Under Hosted + BAA we'll treat KV as in-scope but can limit lifetime to the session only and ensure it is zeroed at session end.

- Suggested minimal pilot config: Hosted + edge-sidecar for aggressive PII redaction, 30-day request log retention negotiated in BAA, and in-memory encryption of KV. If you want us to host the scrubber we can propose a scoped managed add-on.

Happy to sketch the scrubber config and the runtime flags in a short runbook.

—Dylan
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Beck <sara@baastream.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Inquiry — BAA coverage for clinical pipeline (tokenization + retention)

Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed. Quick confirmations:

- We'll plan Hosted pilot with our sidecar + Redwood edge scrubber (dual layer) and negotiate 30-day retention in the BAA.
- Please upload the evidence pack + redacted SOC 2 to the HubSpot company record and share NDA if required; Roberto will coordinate legal.
- For the pilot statement-of-work, can you include an option line-item for "Redwood-hosted scrubber" vs "Customer-hosted sidecar" so we can budget both?

Let's schedule 30m on Friday to align the pilot kickoff and get the draft BAA in front of legal. I'll send a meeting invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sara
Director of Product, Baastream
